page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without hyperthreading, alongside 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, achieving an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local NVMe SSD instance storage provides 5,700 GB of high-speed capacity, complemented by a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system does not include discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and memory throughput. The server scores in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng (163,906.36) and Geekbench multi-core (26,336.0), driven by its full suite of 96 dedicated physical cores. Uncached read memory bandwidth reaches 481.68 GB/sec with uncached writes at 218.19 GB/sec, placing memory operations squarely in the top 10%. Database and in-memory operations exhibit notable velocity, achieving 201.15 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks alongside high PassMark database operation scores. Static web serving throughput also achieves top-tier rates at 160.17 GB/sec.

Single-core performance falls within average ranges, as seen in single-core stress-ng (1,709.79) and single-core Geekbench (1,906.0). Software execution without deep multi-threading or hardware acceleration will not fully utilize this machine profile. Additionally, small-model LLM text generation shows lower throughput (35.42 tokens/sec), reflecting the absence of specialized accelerators. However, the density of physical cores, 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, and 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage deliver significant resource efficiency for massive scale-out and memory-bound jobs.

Given its hardware topology and benchmark characteristics, AWS r8gd.metal-24xl is best suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput database systems, large compilation workloads, and intensive data processing operations that demand bare-metal access and high memory bandwidth.

It features 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM (8.0 GB per core), 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 40 Gbps network interface, without discrete GPUs. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute, high memory bandwidth (481.68 GB/sec uncached reads), and outstanding database performance, recording 201.15 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. While single-thread execution and unaccelerated small-model LLM generation register in average to lower percentiles, its 96 non-hyperthreaded physical cores and massive memory capacity provide strong resource efficiency for concurrent operations. The server is ideal for in-memory databases, distributed caching, massive compilation pipelines, and heavy transactional database workloads.
